vuln_id: ARVO arvo:31425 / LibreDWG Classes sentinel over-read

staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot. Its `src/decode.c:1109` line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer trace, while the sample metadata names earlier still-vulnerable commit `1b908d0d9eb2da3ada7f1f3caf067fc0041dfc3d`.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the decode_R13_2000 function in the decode module, where invalid classes are not properly checked.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 72-byte DWG witness is accepted as `AC1013` and dispatched to `decode_R13_R2000()`. Its section locator table decodes `num_sections = 7`, then materializes the Classes slot (`section[1]`) with `address = 72` and `size = 0`. The existing section-table check only rejects `address + size > dat->size`, so this zero-length one-past-end Classes section passes because `72 + 0` is not greater than the 72-byte file length. Later the Classes parser copies that address into `dat->byte` and immediately executes `memcmp(dwg_sentinel(...), &dat->chain[dat->byte], 16)` to probe the class-begin sentinel without checking that 16 bytes are readable from the chosen offset. Because `dat->byte == dat->size == 72`, the sentinel probe reads 16 bytes from the one-past-end pointer and AddressSanitizer reports a heap-buffer-overflow READ in `decode_R13_R2000` at `src/decode.c:1109`. The staged patch fixes the witnessed path by skipping the Classes section when `dat->byte +16 > dat->size` or the section extent exceeds the input.

source.value_from: The exact staged 72-byte `poc`; after `dwg_decode()` admits the `AC1013` header, the section-locator count field at offset `0x15` is consumed here and decodes to `7`.
source.description: First project-code materialization of vulnerability-relevant parser state on the witnessed path. The decoded section count drives allocation and iteration of the section locator table, ensuring slot 1 is parsed as the later-used Classes descriptor.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `memcmp` consumes 16 bytes from `&dat->chain[72]`, which is the one-past-end pointer for the 72-byte fuzz input buffer.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable Classes-entry path copies the attacker-controlled section start into `dat->byte` and then proceeds to the sentinel probe without the patch's missing rejection `dat->byte +16 > dat->size`, so a one-past-end section start is treated as if a 16-byte sentinel were available.

tainted_value_origin.description: This section-locator field becomes the Classes read cursor. On the staged PoC, the `j == 1` record decodes to address `72`, which is exactly the file length.
tainted_value_origin.note: The decoder later hard-codes slot 1 as `SECTION_CLASSES_R13`, so this parsed value is copied into `dat->byte` immediately before the crashing sentinel `memcmp`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness begins with the valid DWG version code `AC1013`, so `dwg_decode()` routes it into the exact vulnerable parser `decode_R13_R2000()` instead of rejecting it as non-DWG input.

fine_trace.note: The harness wraps the staged `poc` as a `Bit_Chain`. The saved witness is a 72-byte DWG file beginning with `AC1013`, and ASan reports the invalid read 0 bytes to the right of the same 72-byte heap region supplied by libFuzzer.

After `dwg_decode()` dispatches the `AC1013` file to `decode_R13_R2000()`, the section locator count decodes to `7`. This count drives the section-array allocation and ensures the loop reads slot `j == 1`, which the decoder later treats as the Classes section.

On the `j == 1` iteration, the second section record yields Classes address `72`. Because the witness length is also 72 bytes, this parsed offset is already the one-past-end cursor that later becomes `dat->byte` at Classes entry.
The same Classes section record sets `size = 0`, so the parsed section extent is `72 + 0`.

The only existing section-table bounds check is `address + size > dat->size`. For the witnessed record this becomes `72 + 0 > 72`, which is false, so the zero-length one-past-end Classes slot is accepted instead of being rejected before Classes parsing.

Classes parsing copies the accepted tainted address into `dat->byte`, so the read cursor becomes `72`, the first byte past the buffer. Unlike the staged patch, the vulnerable path does not reject `dat->byte +16 > dat->size` before the upcoming 16-byte sentinel probe.

ASan sink. `memcmp` reads 16 bytes starting at `&dat->chain[72]`; because the 72-byte input ends at that address, the read starts from the one-past-end pointer and triggers the reported heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 16.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds the missing pre-sentinel rejection at Classes entry: if `dat->byte +16 > dat->size` or the Classes section extent exceeds `dat->size`, the parser skips the Classes section instead of calling `memcmp` on `&dat->chain[dat->byte]`. For the witnessed PoC, `dat->byte` is `72`, so that new check stops the crash before the sentinel probe.
sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from the staged vulnerable source snapshot, `patch.diff`, `sanitizer_trace.txt`, `reproduction_report.json`, and a source-faithful static decode of the saved 72-byte PoC section locator fields

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: The ASan allocation is the 72-byte libFuzzer input buffer, and the trace's attacker-controlled Classes address `72` explains why the project sink starts reading exactly at that allocation's upper bound.

format.name: AutoCAD Release 13c3 DWG
format.contract: The exact 72-byte DWG witness must parse as `AC1013`, decode `num_sections = 7`, and give the Classes slot `section[1]` the pair `address = 72`, `size = 0`, so `decode_R13_R2000()` reaches the class-begin sentinel probe and executes `memcmp(..., &dat->chain[72], 16)` on a 72-byte input.
